stories.title: AI Wealth Management Platform Vise Grabs 12K SF at 50 Ninth Avenue
stories.excerpt: Artificial intelligence-powered wealth management platform Vise is moving from SoHo to 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District, where it will quadruple its office space to 11,949 square feet. The space spans the second floor of several combined historic townhomes along the Ninth Avenue frontage and therefore has dramatic, over 20 foot-high pitched ceilings and an atrium outdoor garden. Rob Kluge and Brandon Charnas of Current Real Estate Advisors represented the tenant in the 10-year lease. Howard Hersch, Greg Conen, Jennifer Schreiber and Natalie Serio of Newmark represented the building owner, Tavros Capital, which will build out the space. The asking rent was $150 per square foot. Vise is an AI-driven wealth management platform for independent advisors founded by Samir Vasavada and Runik Mehrotra that launched in November 2019. It hosts over $100 billion in assets and the firm is reported to be valued at over $22 billion. It is currently located in 4,000 square feet of office space at 521 Broadway in SoHo. In searching for new digs, Vise was focused on upgrading both its office and culture. “We worked with ownership on a creative solution whereby the ground-floor retailer, Jen Rubio’s fashion company — now known as Elsa, which was then negotiating their deal — would expand upstairs and take roughly another 4,000 to 5,000 square feet on the West 14th Street side of the floor,” Charnas said. “That allowed us to create a space for Vise that fit both their program and their budget.” “We worked through multiple iterations with ownership and the architect to take what had been one larger floor and create the right long-term home for Vise,” added Kluge. The resulting space primarily overlooks Ninth Avenue and sits directly across from the Apple store, with dramatic vaulted ceilings, tons of light and a build-out being designed specifically around Vise’s needs and specifications. bullets: Vise AI platform leases 11,949 SF at 50 Ninth Ave, Meatpacking District Manhattan.
Tenant quadruples office footprint from 4,000 SF; 10-year lease at $150/SF.
Vise valued at $22B+, manages $100B+ AUM; signals strong tech hiring in NYC.
stories.summary: Vise, an AI-powered wealth management platform valued at $22 billion and managing over $100 billion in assets, is expanding its Manhattan office by 300% to 11,949 square feet at 50 Ninth Avenue in the Meatpacking District. The company signed a 10-year lease at $150 per square foot, moving from its 4,000-square-foot SoHo space. The expansion signals strong growth and hiring appetite among high-value fintech firms in New York City.
stories.impact: Strong multifamily demand signal for Manhattan. Fintech and AI-sector expansions typically precede wave hiring and junior employee in-migration; watch for rental demand surge in West Village, Chelsea, and Meatpacking submarkets as support staff and early-career professionals relocate to NYC for these roles.

stories.title: Friedman Real Estate Completes Transition, Onboarding of 1.2M-SF Illinois Commercial Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Friedman Real Estate announced the successful onboarding and transition of a 1.2 million-square-foot portfolio of retail, office, and industrial properties throughout Illinois during the first half of 2026. This includes 290,000 square feet on Michigan Avenue, as well as properties in suburbs like Highland Park, Northbrook, Evanston, and Downer’s Grove. The successful Illinois portfolio transition further strengthens Friedman’s growing presence throughout key Midwest markets, including Michigan, Illinois, Indiana, Ohio, and Wisconsin. The comprehensive transition included onboarding multiple assets, implementing operational and financial reporting systems, coordinating with vendors, communicating with tenants, conducting compliance reviews, and establishing property-specific management strategies to enhance asset performance and support long-term ownership objectives. “Our growth throughout Illinois and the broader Midwest reflects a simple philosophy: deliver results, provide responsive service, and act as a true partner to our clients,” said Karin Meier, Senior Managing Director of Friedman Real Estate Commercial Management and Facilities. The post Friedman Real Estate Completes Transition, Onboarding of 1.2M-SF Illinois Commercial Portfolio appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Friedman RE onboards 1.2M SF commercial portfolio across Illinois suburbs; 290K SF on Michigan Ave.
Portfolio includes retail, office, industrial; properties in Highland Park, Northbrook, Evanston, Downers Grove.
Signals Midwest institutional capital consolidation and property management professionalization in key markets.
stories.summary: Friedman Real Estate completed the transition and onboarding of 1.2 million square feet of mixed-use commercial properties across Illinois during the first half of 2026, including significant Michigan Avenue exposure and suburban assets in Highland Park, Northbrook, Evanston, and Downers Grove. The company strengthened its footprint across the broader Midwest, including Michigan, Indiana, Ohio, and Wisconsin. The transition involved comprehensive operational restructuring and tenant coordination.
stories.impact: Limited direct multifamily relevance. However, Friedman's growing Midwest presence and operational focus signal institutional capital aggregating commercial real estate across Midwest metros. Watch for potential Friedman entry into multifamily if platform expands; Midwest suburban office-to-residential conversions may accelerate if Friedman identifies underperforming office assets.

stories.title: Capital Group Expands Plaza District Footprint with New Lease at 345 Park Ave.
stories.excerpt: Capital Group, the world’s largest active global investment manager, is adding a new office at Rudin’s 345 Park Ave. in Midtown Manhattan’s Plaza District. The firm will occupy the entire 70,400-square-foot fourth floor of 345 Park in a 10-year lease and will move in during the fall of 2027 while maintaining its current space at 399 Park Ave. Founded in 1931, Capital Group now manages $3.6 trillion in assets for millions of wealth management and institutional clients around the world from 34 offices that house more than 9,000 employees. “345 Park Ave.’s prime location, large floor plates, and our upcoming amenity enhancements distinguish it as a best-in-class asset,” said Michael Rudin, Co-CEO at Rudin. “We are pleased to accommodate Capital Group’s continued growth in the Plaza District and commitment to New York City.” Robert Steinman, SVP of office leasing, represented Rudin in-house. Chris Mansfield, Frank Scott, David Opper, Zachary Weil, Eddie Sisca and Trevor Larkin of CBRE represented Capital Group. The post Capital Group Expands Plaza District Footprint with New Lease at 345 Park Ave. appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: Capital Group leases entire 70,400 SF fourth floor at 345 Park Ave, Midtown Manhattan.
10-year lease; move-in fall 2027; world's largest active investment manager ($3.6T AUM).
Maintains 399 Park Ave space; signals institutional capital commitment to Plaza District office.
stories.summary: Capital Group, the world's largest active investment manager with $3.6 trillion in assets under management, is expanding its Manhattan footprint by leasing the entire 70,400-square-foot fourth floor at 345 Park Avenue in Midtown's Plaza District. The 10-year lease begins fall 2027, and the firm will retain its existing 399 Park Avenue space. The expansion demonstrates continued institutional investor confidence in premium Manhattan office.
stories.impact: Modest indirect multifamily impact. Capital Group's expansion signals sustained institutional hiring and real estate bullishness in Midtown, but office expansion does not directly drive residential demand in the way corporate relocations do. However, the reaffirmation of 345 Park Ave's trophy-asset status may stabilize cap rates for nearby mixed-use development and signal sustained Plaza District residential appeal for high-income households.

stories.title: JLL Arranges $42M Fannie Mae Refinancing for Portland-Area Multifamily
stories.excerpt: JLL has arranged $42 million in financing for Portola Bridge Creek, a 270-unit, garden-style apartment community in Vancouver, Washington. JLL worked on behalf of the borrower, SB Real Estate Partners (SBREP), which has owned the property since 2022, to secure the five-year, fixed-rate loan through Fannie Mae. The JLL Capital Markets Debt Advisory team representing the borrower was led by Executive Managing Director Charles Halladay, Senior Director Rick Salinas and Director Elijah Lax. Built in 1989, Portola Bridge Creek offers one-, two- and three-bedroom floor plans ranging from 650 to 1,150 square feet. The property is located at 9211 NE 15th Ave., in the Hazel Dell North area of Vancouver. The property sits just nine miles north of Downtown Portland and only six miles north of the Vancouver Waterfront redevelopment. JLL also arranged a four-pack, $110 million Freddie Mac refinance on behalf of SBREP in September of 2025. The conversations behind tomorrow’s apartment deals happen at Connect Apartments on September 22 in LA. Connect with the capital sources, owners, developers, and brokers driving multifamily investment. Learn more and reserve your seat at www.connectapts2026.com. The post JLL Arranges $42M Fannie Mae Refinancing for Portland-Area Multifamily appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: JLL arranges $42M Fannie Mae five-year fixed-rate refinance for Portola Bridge Creek, Vancouver WA.
270-unit garden-style apartment community; SB Real Estate Partners borrower; owned since 2022.
Property 9 miles north of Downtown Portland, 6 miles from Vancouver Waterfront redevelopment.
stories.summary: JLL arranged a $42 million, five-year fixed-rate Fannie Mae refinance for Portola Bridge Creek, a 270-unit garden-style apartment community in Vancouver, Washington, on behalf of borrower SB Real Estate Partners. The property, built in 1989 and offering one-, two-, and three-bedroom units ranging from 650 to 1,150 square feet, is located in Hazel Dell North, nine miles north of Downtown Portland. This follows SBREP's $110 million Freddie Mac refinance on a four-property portfolio in September 2025.
stories.impact: Refinancing availability signals continued multifamily capital-markets appetite despite rate environment. Vancouver WA (just north of Portland) is a secondary-market proxy for Portland metro growth. Repeated Fannie Mae and Freddie Mac execution suggests stabilizing loan markets; watch for development pipeline reactivation in Portland-Vancouver corridor as builder confidence returns and construction financing becomes more accessible.

stories.title: SME Capital Forced to Hand Over Hudson Yards Condo Building to Residents
stories.excerpt: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is handing ownership of 441 West 37th Street to the condominium board after an investigation by the New York Attorney General’s office. SME acquired the building out of foreclosure in 2023. It then failed to pay bills related to the Hudson Yards property and neglected safety violations, leading to a settlement to pay $700,000, according to Attorney General Letitia James. Built in 2020 by Levi Balkany, the nine-unit building went into foreclosure in 2023. SME never reported to the state that it was the winning bidder in the auction and never acknowledged that it owned the building, leaving residents to pick up the tab for things like a new $15,824 certificate of occupancy, according to the AG. Some of the units were rented out while awaiting buyers, including 35 formerly homeless people who were ousted around the time SME took control of the building, according to The Real Deal. “Private equity firms do not get to pick and choose which laws apply to them,” James said in a statement. “When this company took control of a Manhattan condo building, it took on real legal responsibilities to the homeowners who lived there. For two years, SME Capital dodged those duties while still collecting rent checks. My office will keep holding these firms accountable when they put profits over New Yorkers’ safety.” Balkany could not be reached for comment. bullets: SME Capital forced to transfer 441 West 37th St, Hudson Yards nine-unit condo to residents.
Property acquired in foreclosure 2023; failed to pay bills, violated safety codes; $700K settlement.
NY AG Letitia James enforcement; previously housed 35 formerly homeless residents later evicted.
stories.summary: Private investment firm SME Capital Ventures is relinquishing ownership of 441 West 37th Street, a nine-unit condominium building in Hudson Yards, to the condo board following an investigation by New York Attorney General Letitia James. SME acquired the property out of foreclosure in 2023, then failed to pay bills, neglected safety violations, and improperly failed to report its ownership to the state. The firm settled by paying $700,000; the building had previously housed 35 homeless residents who were displaced.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily development impact. However, the enforcement action signals tightened regulatory scrutiny of distressed-asset acquisition and management in NYC, particularly regarding Section 8 and homeless-housing conversions. Developers should expect elevated compliance and transparency requirements when acquiring foreclosed or subsidized properties in New York; reputational risk and AG enforcement may cool aggressive distressed-play strategies.

stories.title: SRS Real Estate Partners Brokers $15M Sale of Retail Property Anchored by Chick-fil-A
stories.excerpt: SRS Real Estate Partners completed the $14.95 million sale of a two-tenant retail property located at 540 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Virginia, about 15 miles from Washington, D.C. Built in 2019 and situated on 1.19 acres, this unique two-story property is fully occupied by Chick-fil-A on the ground floor with a drive-thru. Flagship Carwash is operating a full-service facility on the second floor. SRS Capital Markets Executive Vice President & Managing Principal Andrew Fallon and First Vice President Philip Wellde represented the seller, the property’s original developer. The buyer was a local investor. “As a net lease investment offering, the asset attracted significant interest from a wide range of investors, including high-net-worth and 1031 exchange buyers seeking a high-quality property with long-term passive income and a building that has tax-efficient components,” said Fallon. Located at 540 Maple Avenue East, the property benefits from a premier infill location in the heart of Vienna. bullets: SRS RE Partners brokers $14.95M sale of two-tenant retail property, Vienna VA near Washington DC.

stories.summary: SRS Real Estate Partners completed the $14.95 million sale of a two-story retail property at 540 Maple Avenue in Vienna, Virginia, about 15 miles from Washington, D.C. The 1.19-acre asset, built in 2019, is fully leased to Chick-fil-A (ground floor with drive-thru) and Flagship Carwash (second floor). A local investor acquired the net-lease property, which attracted significant interest from 1031 exchange and high-net-worth buyers seeking stable, tax-efficient income.
stories.impact: Minimal multifamily relevance. Retail net-lease activity does not signal residential demand; however, Vienna's continued appeal for well-capitalized real estate investors and 1031 buyers suggests stable equity availability in the DC exurban market. Multifamily developers should monitor Vienna/Loudoun submarket for single-family rental and townhome conversion opportunities as local capital remains active.

stories.title: PRP Real Assets Acquires 900 19th Street NW in DC
stories.excerpt: PRP Real Assets, a Washington, D.C.–based real estate investment management firm, has acquired 900 19th Street NW, a 116,385-square-foot office tower in the heart of the city’s Central Business District. Positioned at the corner of 19th and Eye Streets, between K Street and Pennsylvania Avenue, the corner building sits three blocks west of the White House, steps from the Farragut West Metro station, and within walking distance of the World Bank and International Monetary Fund headquarters. The previous owner completed a comprehensive base-building and aesthetic redevelopment of the property. “900 19th Street is exactly the kind of asset we look for in the current market, an institutionally repositioned building in the most durable corridor in the District, acquired at a basis that cannot be replicated through new construction,” said Jon McAvoy, Chief Investment Officer of PRP Real Assets. The post PRP Real Assets Acquires 900 19th Street NW in DC appeared first on Connect CRE.
bullets: PRP Real Assets acquires 900 19th St NW, DC; 116,385 SF office tower in CBD.
Prime location: corner of 19th and Eye Streets, 3 blocks west of White House.
Acquired at basis unreplicable via new construction; prior owner completed full redevelopment.
stories.summary: PRP Real Assets, a Washington, D.C.–based investment firm, acquired 900 19th Street NW, a 116,385-square-foot office tower in the heart of the city's Central Business District. Positioned at the corner of 19th and Eye Streets between K Street and Pennsylvania Avenue, three blocks west of the White House and steps from the Farragut West Metro station, the building was recently redeveloped by the prior owner. PRP cited the acquisition basis as unreplicable through new construction.
stories.impact: Minimal direct multifamily impact. However, institutional capital pursuing fully repositioned, prime-location office assets at deep discounts to replacement cost suggests DC CBD office cap rates are compressing and valuations are stabilizing. This may signal end of office distress; watch for mixed-use redevelopment window closing in DC as office assets stabilize, reducing conversion opportunities for developers.

stories.title: Sisters of the Visitation Monastery Sells to Integritas Capital for $42M
stories.excerpt: A 170-year-old monastery in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, has sold for $42.25 million. The Sisters of the Visitation’s 7.5-acre campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard — a campus behind 30-foot stone walls, with a monastery, chapel and school — was bought by a group of Brooklyn-based developers and investors with a history of large residential projects, including leaders of Integritas Capital and Heights Advisors. A petition by the Catholic religious order to sell its real estate was approved by the office of the New York State Attorney General on Monday. Nonprofits are required by New York law to obtain approval when it sells all or most of its assets. The buyer entity, 1137 91 LLC, is led by Brooklyn real estate investor Stephen Palmese, founder of private equity platform Integritas Capital (and a former vice chair at JLL). Passive investors included Rachel Foster, founder and president of Brooklyn housing developer Heights Advisors, alongside the developer’s director, Scott Geddes, as well as Daniel Kodsi and Matthew Kodsi . The longtime professional partners are planning a resort-residential tower in Fort Lauderdale, according to The Real Deal. Palmese’s Integritas is also the lender behind a forthcoming 27-story church-to-residential conversion in Brooklyn’s Fort Greene. The cohort of buyers suggests the historic property’s likely fate as a major mixed-used or residential development. The Visitation Sisters entered into an initial contract in late April, according to the filing, but the school and monastery have been shuttered since 2024, after their numbers dropped too low to sustain full ministry. The Visitation Sisters, formally the Order of the Visitation of Holy Mary, were a French order founded in 1610. Their presence in Brooklyn dates back to 1855. The sellers expect net proceeds of $40.9 million, according to the filing, which will be held in escrow under an approved dissolution and distribution of assets plan. bullets: Sisters of the Visitation sell 7.5-acre monastery campus, Bay Ridge Brooklyn, for $42.25M.
170-year-old property sold to Integritas Capital-led group; includes monastery, chapel, school behind 30-foot walls.
Buyer has history of large residential projects; NY AG approval required for nonprofit asset sale.
stories.summary: The Sisters of the Visitation sold their 170-year-old, 7.5-acre monastery campus at 8902 Ridge Boulevard in Bay Ridge, Brooklyn, for $42.25 million to an investor group led by Integritas Capital founder Stephen Palmese and Heights Advisors founder Rachel Foster. The portfolio includes a monastery, chapel, and school. The sale required approval from the New York State Attorney General, as state law requires nonprofits to obtain permission when selling all or most assets.
stories.impact: High-value signal for Brooklyn multifamily developers. A 7.5-acre, fully controlled, residential-zoned land parcel in Bay Ridge at ~$5.6M per acre suggests strong Brooklyn investor appetite and development feasibility. Watch for mixed-use residential (and possibly conversion) announcements; the buyer's track record with large residential projects indicates intention to develop. Bay Ridge's affordability premium and transit access (relative to Williamsburg/Park Slope) make this site attractive for moderate-income multifamily; monitor for zoning variance or City planning signals.

stories.title: Benefit Street Partners Provides $103M Bridge Debt for Texas Multifamily Portfolio
stories.excerpt: Vantage Communities has secured $103 million in bridge debt to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio in three cities in Texas, Commercial Observer can first report. Benefit Street Partners provided the debt, which will finance the property toward full stabilization and is structured as a floating-rate, interest-only bridge loan with a three-year term. Greystone Capital Advisors‘ Drew Fletcher, Bryan Grover, Jesse Kopecky and Cameron Behr arranged the transaction. “Benefit Street Partners recognized the quality of the sponsorship, the assets, and the long-term fundamentals supporting these dynamic Central Texas markets,” said Fletcher. The three assets are split among Vantage at Hutto — a 288-unit complex located at 1051 North Farm to Market 1660 in Hutto, Tex., just outside of Austin; Vantage at McKinney Falls — a 288-unit complex located at 7900 McKinney Falls Parkway in suburban Austin, Tex.; and Vantage at Fair Oaks — a 288-unit complex located at 9135 Dietz Elkhorn Road in Boerne, Tex. outside of San Antonio. All three assets opened in either 2023 or 2024 and feature amenities such as resident clubhouses, fitness centers and resort-style swimming pools. “We were pleased to structure a financing solution that met our clients’ objectives while leveraging the strength of this high-quality, recently delivered portfolio,” added Fletcher in a statement. Brian Pascus can be reached at bpascus@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Benefit Street Partners provides $103M bridge debt for Vantage Communities three-property, 864-unit Texas portfolio.
Properties in Hutto, McKinney Falls (Austin suburbs), and Boerne; floating-rate, interest-only, three-year term.
Greystone Capital Advisors arranged; bridges assets toward stabilization in dynamic Central Texas markets.
stories.summary: Vantage Communities secured $103 million in floating-rate, interest-only bridge debt from Benefit Street Partners to refinance a three-property, 864-unit multifamily portfolio across Central Texas. The portfolio includes Vantage at Hutto (288 units), Vantage at McKinney Falls (288 units, Austin suburbs), and a third property in Boerne, structured for a three-year term to finance the portfolio toward full stabilization. Greystone Capital Advisors arranged the transaction.
stories.impact: Bridge-debt execution signals strong Central Texas multifamily fundamentals and lender confidence in stabilization paths. Austin metro continues attracting capital; bridge financing (vs. permanent) suggests these assets are not yet at full occupancy or rent growth, but lenders are bullish on near-term lease-up. Watch for these three-properties' exit timing (24-36 months); successful stabilization will reinforce Austin as magnet for institutional multifamily capital and likely trigger new development starts in Hutto and McKinney Falls submarkets.

stories.title: Coastland Residential Lands $85M to Build Miami-Dade Rental
stories.excerpt: Coastland Residential has nabbed a $84.5 million construction loan for a multifamily development near Tropical Park in southwest Miami-Dade County. The debt from PNC Bank covers the Vybe 75, which will house 366 apartments and 5,000 square feet of ground-floor retail space. The eight-story development at 4383 Southwest 75th Avenue sits just east of Tropical Park and the Palmetto Expressway, south of Bird Road. At least a portion of the units will be priced within 120 percent of the area’s median income, though a representative for the Pinecrest-based developer declined to provide an exact figure. Amenities will include a rooftop pool, a gym, a co-working lounge, a sports simulator and a movie theater. Coastland Residential purchased the 4.3-acre site for $14.5 million last year, according to property records. The Corwil Architects-designed development represents the first phase of a larger project that’s expected to deliver about 1,000 units in total. Launched five years ago by Anthony Seijas and Alejandro Rodriguez, Coastland Residential grew out of Rodriguez’s contracting and construction management firm, Coastland Construction, which is also serving as the contractor for Vybe 75. Julia Echikson can be reached at jechikson@commercialobserver.com.
bullets: Coastland Residential secures $84.5M PNC Bank construction loan for Vybe 75, Miami-Dade, 366 units.
Eight-story development at 4383 Southwest 75th Ave, near Tropical Park; ground-floor retail.
Developer purchased 4.3-acre site for $14.5M; Phase 1 of ~1,000-unit master project; portion affordable at 120% AMI.
stories.summary: Coastland Residential obtained an $84.5 million construction loan from PNC Bank for Vybe 75, an eight-story, 366-unit multifamily development in southwest Miami-Dade County near Tropical Park. The project at 4383 Southwest 75th Avenue includes 5,000 square feet of ground-floor retail and a portion of units priced within 120 percent of area median income. Coastland purchased the 4.3-acre site for $14.5 million and plans the development as Phase 1 of a larger ~1,000-unit master project.
stories.impact: Strong Miami-Dade supply and capital signal. $84.5M construction financing at scale indicates PNC and lenders regained confidence in Miami development; this is Phase 1 of 1,000 units total, signaling sustained builder appetite and capitalization in Miami. Southwest Miami-Dade (Tropical Park submarket) is emerging secondary location; monitor absorption and rent growth here as Post-hurricane construction activity unfolds and supply arrives. Watch for Phase 2 announcement within 12–18 months; if absorbed well, signals shift in Miami multifamily demand southwestward from Brickell/Edgewater.
